UPSTREAM: Revert "libpayload: Reset PS/2 keyboard" Documentation is scarce on the matter, however the related coreboot code suggests that after the ACK, the keyboard also sends the result of the self test (passed/failed). It looks like this result is never consumed here, probably resulting in further confusion for later com- mands. Let's revert this for now (if it's not too late for the 4.10 release) and break things later again. IMHO, due to the fact that there are dozens of different keyboard controller and keyboard implementations and no accurate specification followed, such changes should be tested on a lot of hardware before merge. This reverts commit a99ed13e3397bc536012120aab8cadb827913863. This reverts commit 7ae606f57f0b3d450ae748141b0e2367041b27d3. UPSTREAM: soc/amd/stoneyridge: Move GPIO support to common The banked GPIO functionality in the AcpiMmio block has been consistent since the Mullins product. Move the basic support into a common directory. Each product's pin availability, MUXes, and other details must remain specific to the product. The relocated source also drops the weak configure_gevent_smi() that reports SMI is not available. The stoneyridge port relies on SMI to do its initialization, similar to modern soc/intel devices. This is the plan for future soc/amd ports, so make a missing function a build error instead of a runtime warning. UPSTREAM: ec/google/wilco: Add UCSI support This change adds support for the UCSI specification in order to provide information about the Type-C port and an interface to perform power and data role swap. This change is split across the DSDT and SSDT, with the shared memory and operation region declared in the SSDT after being allocated in CBMEM. The OS will fill in the registers in the system memory region and then call the _DSM method wtih a read or write argument. The DSM method will copy the required registers to/from the system memory and the EC and perform the write or read action. Responses from the EC will generate a new SCI with event code 0x79 which will notify this UCSI ACPI device and the OS driver will take action to read status from the EC. CHROMIUM: go2001: Don't immediately wait for replies to (most) messages. To allow for more parallelism, don't wait for messages to be replied to from the point of where they are queued. Instead, queue them and return immediately. To be able to do this, we need an ability to queue messages and not wait for them to be sent to hardware (while the ring buffer is full), which requires pending message memory to be managed separately. Switch to allocating their buffers dynamically. To make this more optimal, use kmem_cache. Messages are allocated when queued to be send to hardware, and freed after copied to the ring buffer, or on error, if still pending at that point. Given that VM_EMPTY_BUFFER messages are scheduled in the interrupt context, their memory has to be allocated beforehand. Do this by allocating in buf_prepare callback and storing the memory on source go2001_buffer. Not waiting for VM_EMPTY_BUFFER messages introduces an additional complication on resolution change. When receiving a resolution change notification in reply from hardware, we may have additional messages pending already, which will be processed and returned to us from hardware with a request to reprocess them after handling the resolution change. To handle this, move all buffers that hardware requested to be reprocessed to a new resume queue. After the resolution change sequence is finished, move them back in front of the source queue for reprocessing. This also requires us to allocate another message buffer for reprocessing at that time. Finally, waiting for context to be finished now involves waiting for the pending message queue to become empty (i.e. messages are moved to the outgoing message ring buffer), followed by waiting for replies to all these messages to arrive from hardware. CHROMIUM: go2001: Remove periodic intra refresh. Sets initial rate control settings instead of relying on hard-coded settings in firmware. This sets QP min/max thresholds to current libvpx ones and explicitly disables periodic intra and buffer refreshes. Disabling periodic refreshes show a significant SSIM/PSNR increase and fewer bitrate spikes (due to keyframes which are more expensive). They were previously enabled/hard-coded due to a race condition in RTCVideoEncoder where two consecutive frames could have the exact same RTP timestamp if they get queued up, causing one of them to be dropped and the bitstream would not be decodable from now on. RTP timestamps are now based on input timestamps (which are never duplicate as they would then have been dropped by WebRTC before reaching the encoder). BUG=chromium:700042 TEST=Manual SSIM/PSNR comparison and running Hangouts for an hour. CHROMIUM: bluetooth: clean up connection in hci_cs_disconnect In bluetooth core specification 4.2, Vol 2, Part E, 7.8.9 LE Set Advertise Enable Command, it says The Controller shall continue advertising until ... or until a connection is created or ... In these cases, advertising is then disabled. Hence, advertising would be disabled before a connection is established. In current kernel implementation, advertising would be re-enabled when all connections are terminated. The correct disconnection flow looks like < HCI Command: Disconnect > HCI Event: Command Status Status: Success > HCI Event: Disconnect Complete Status: Success Specifically, the last Disconnect Complete Event would trigger a callback function hci_event.c:hci_disconn_complete_evt() to cleanup the connection and re-enable advertising when proper. However, sometimes, there might occur an exception in the controller when disconnection is being executed. The disconnection flow might then look like < HCI Command: Disconnect > HCI Event: Command Status Status: Unknown Connection Identifier Note that "> HCI Event: Disconnect Complete" is missing when such an exception occurs. This would result in advertising staying disabled forever since the connection in question is not cleaned up correctly. To fix the controller exception issue, we need to do some connection cleanup when the disconnect command status indicates an error. BUG=b:70903583 TEST=Run magic tethering without a SIM card. Sometimes, an "Unknown Connection Identifier" controller error would show up in the disconnect command status event in the btsnoop log. This would end up with the missing of Disconnect Complete Event which looks like < HCI Command: Disconnect (0x01|0x0006) plen 3 [hci0] 17:23:55.037679 Handle: 3585 Reason: Remote User Terminated Connection (0x13) > HCI Event: Command Status (0x0f) plen 4 [hci0] 17:23:55.038612 Disconnect (0x01|0x0006) ncmd 1 Status: Unknown Connection Identifier (0x02) @ MGMT Event: Command Compl.. (0x0001) plen 10 [hci0] 17:23:55.038663 Disconnect (0x0014) plen 7 Status: Not Connected (0x02) LE Address: 76:1D:6E:C2:5B:AC (Resolvable) However, observe that the advertising would still be re-enabled as follows < HCI Command: LE Set Advertise... (0x08|0x000a) [hci0] 17:23:55.141659 Advertising: Enabled (0x01) Change-Id: Id25cec6532ade569a87e7c6f24061219855e08a6 Signed-off-by: Joseph Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1053041 Commit-Ready: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1644243 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org>

bluetooth: "Fix" sync of commands for adv & scan This is a very ugly hack, presented here in a very ugly way. The ugly way is basically how we deliver this only for eve and not affect other devices. The ugly hack is basically how we work aroung bluez's complete lack of synchronization. Let me explain. No, there is not time. Let me summarize: bluez has a boolean value for "are we scanning" which it updates inside the command-complete event handler. It also checks this in many places as a way to tell if the chip is or is not scanning. The issue is that some chips (like BCM's) let you disable something already disabled and do not raise a fuss. Other chips (like Intel's 7265) do raise a fuss if you try to disable scanning if it is already off. So why the issue? If the chip raises an error, bluez loses its marbles and gets out of sync with the chip. Basically it thinks the chip *IS* scanning while chip is not. There is no way out of this since any attempt to tell bluez to start scanning causes it to just reply with "already am" and any attempt to stop scanning sends the "scan disable" command to the chip and produces the same kind of error that got us into this mess. So how do we fix this? There isn't really a simple or elegant way. But the basic issue is that while a command to enable or disable scanning is in flight, any code in the stack will think scanning is still in the old state, while it may already be in the new state. This might cause more commands to be enqueued based on this errorneous information. To solve this we'd like to always have correct information. Sadly this is not easy. There is also a command queue, which at any point in time may have many command enqueued that affect scanning state. There are multiple ways to insert commands into it, and we do not want to instrument them all. So what do we do? First we add a second boolean bit for "scan state change command in flight". We set this when we *SEND TO THE CHIP* a command that affects scan state and clear it when a reply arrives. We also change all places that check the "are we scanning" state to properly consider this new variable as well. This will not solve the issue of many commands queued already. So it is still possible that while a "disable" was queued, another "disable" may be queued. To work around this we also track the current state in the lowest layer that actually sends commands to the chip and simply drop ones that would transition us to the same state that we're already in. The situation is actually weirder because there is a "restart" func in bluez all of whose callers seem to assume that it atomically toggles scanning off and back on if it is already on. No such atomicity exists in reality. Our hack covers up for this in most cases. Oh, and this same exact logic applies to "are we advertising" boolean and we treat it the same way. This really solves nothing, but it works around the issue well enough for our purposes. A proper fix would be a separate queue for state changes for "adv" and "scan" with proper suport for atomic "restart" requests. This queue would then submit actual commands to the chip's queue. since nobody else would do that, it would have no races. We have no time to produce such fixes, so for now you get to enjoy this dirty hack. This hack is based on initial work by josephsih@ who first figured out the proper place to filter all the low level commands as they are sent to the chip and the proper way to drop them. CHROMIUM: bluetooth: fix a regression about power off delay Conditional commands were introduced to fix run-time race conditions for advertising and scanning. To use conditional commands, all enabling and disabling commands for advertising and scanning are added to the command queue at command build time. And then the command worker thread will check if such a conditional command should be executed or skipped at command run time. This may result in a regression when powering off the bluetooth adapter. When powering off the bluetooth adapter, kernel may send a variety of commands to stop all bluetooth activities and wait for 5 seconds before forcing to power off the adapter. There are two shortcuts to avoid the 5-second long delay. The first shortcut is taken when there are no HCI commands built at all at command built time. The kernel would power off the bluetooth adapter immediately. The second shortcut is taken when the last command of the request is completed. In this case, the clean_up_hci_complete() callback is invoked to power off the bluetooth adapter immediately. The power off regression occurs when the last command in the request is a conditional command and is skipped. In this case, no clean_up_hci_complete() callback would be invoked. The bluetooth adapter cannot be powered off until the 5-second timeout expires. This patch temporarily fixed the regression by adding a dummy command as the last command in the request. This ensures that the clean_up_hci_complete() callback is invoked to power off the bluetooth adapter. As adding a dummy command is kind of hacky, it is desirable to have a formal fix which is being tracked in chromium:808749 Bluez: clean up dummy commands used for conditional HCI command. CHROMIUM: bluetooth: Add a dummy cmd in hci_req_add_le_scan_disable If the HCI_OP_LE_SET_SCAN_ENABLE command is skipped when stopping discovery, the corresponding command complete event would never be received. This would cause the HCI command timeout and thus the stop_discovery method fails. The above said command might be skipped in a rare condition when both kernel and the bluetoothd damemon would like to stop discovery almost at the same time. In this case, chance is that they might be out of sync of the discovery state and result in the above error. To work around the race condtion between kernel and bluetoothd, a dummy HCI command is added. This makes sures that when kernel has stopped scanning at a bit earlier time, bluetoothd, while trying to re-stop discovery and having the HCI command skipped, could still receive the correct stop_discovery_complete callback. tast-tests: network.ConfigureServiceForProfile: grab check_ethernet lock This script stops/starts shill a few times, to reset state and to test that its own state remains across restart. This causes us to lose connectivity briefly, and it gives the recover_duts/check_ethernet.hook infrastructure a chance to start screwing us up. This is particularly problematic if it: * decides to start disabling/re-enabling USB ethernet at the wrong time, as that may prevent our Ethernet Service (that this test looks for) from showing up promptly; or * restarts shill, which will cause us to lose our D-Bus connection and time out Solution: hold the check_ethernet lock for the duration of this test. See also http://crrev.com/c/1637489, which improves the locking on the recover_duts side. Note: even with this lock usage, there is still potentially some ramp-up time after this test, where we are no longer holding the lock but may have brief connectivity loss (while Ethernet is getting re-configured). That's a problem for the next test though ;) Note: shill.Safe{Stop,Start}() utilize the old /run/lock/shill-start.lock properly, but unfortunately this is all pretty racy too, since: (*) check_ethernet.hook doesn't currently acquire the lock -- it only reads it -- so there's still a race window (*) even if shill has started (in the Upstart sense), it may not have finished configuring Ethernet; so check_ethernet.hook may again find the lock "open", but connectivity not in good shape yet This is a problem for another day, requiring total revamp/replacement/removal of shill-start.lock. Fortunately, 'autotest_pause_ethernet_hook' is a sufficient superset of that lock, and it satisfies the needs of this test. I also add the clean-profile-on-exit logic that is present in the Autotest version, but not the Tast version of this test.
